free_tier.stated: a free certificate on every zone, covering the apex and one level of subdomain

per_object_cap.stated: covers example.com and app.example.com, not a.b.example.com; deeper names need Advanced Certificate Manager

retention.stated: the certificate is issued and renewed by Cloudflare while the zone is active

interface_detail: automatic on a proxied zone; no client API of its own, and the zone API reports the certificate
tooling: nothing to run: the certificate appears on the zone
chaining: the certificate half of the free endpoint, from the same account and zone as the DNS and the tunnel

limits.value: one level of subdomain only; deeper names need Advanced Certificate Manager

identity_cost.detail: a Cloudflare account and a zone on Cloudflare nameservers

reliability_note: no suspension, throttle or data-loss event is recorded on the pages read
confidence_note: one-level subdomain coverage, the deeper-subdomain exclusion, the automatic renewal and the paid upgrade path are stated on Cloudflare's own Universal SSL and Limitations pages (both read in full on 2026-11-19), so the limit is first-party documented.

evidence.proved: Universal SSL is free on every plan; the one-level subdomain coverage limit and the Advanced Certificate Manager upgrade path are the substance
on a full setup the certificate covers the apex and first-level subdomains only
evidence.quote: On a full setup, Universal SSL certificates cover your root domain (for example, `example.com`) and first-level subdomains (for example, `www.example.com`).

evidence.proved: Cloudflare's first-party page states full-setup Universal SSL covers the apex and first-level subdomains only
evidence.quote: On a full setup, Universal SSL certificates cover your root domain (for example, `example.com`) and first-level subdomains (for example, `www.example.com`).

evidence.proved: Cloudflare's first-party Limitations page states deeper subdomains are excluded from Universal SSL
evidence.quote: Deeper subdomains — such as `dev.www.example.com` or `app3.dev.www.example.com` — are not covered and will not serve a valid certificate.

evidence.proved: coverage beyond the first subdomain level requires a paid certificate product
evidence.quote: For full setup zones that need coverage beyond first-level subdomains, use Total TLS or advanced certificates.

evidence.proved: Universal SSL is a free certificate issued and renewed automatically for all activated domains
evidence.quote: By default, Cloudflare issues — and renews — free, unshared, publicly trusted SSL certificates to all domains added to and activated on Cloudflare.

evidence.proved: the first-party Limitations page restates the apex plus first-level coverage limit
evidence.quote: When you rely only on Universal SSL in a full setup zone, coverage is limited to the root domain (for example, `example.com`) and first-level subdomains (for example, `www.example.com` or `blog.example.com`).

notes: The one-level limit is the trap. A per-tenant scheme at tenant.app.example.com needs a paid certificate manager, or a wildcard from Let's Encrypt over DNS-01, which is free.
binding_note: full-setup coverage stops at the root domain and first-level subdomains, so a per-tenant name below that level needs the paid Advanced Certificate Manager or Total TLS
